subject: Post-usage settlement guide — Hosted API commits & make-goods
messages:
From: Aisha Geller <aisha.geller@nimblehealth.com>

Subject: Hosted API commit settlement process — next steps and ask

Hi Karthik / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to finalizing the volumes for our Q4 commitment, and Procurement (cc'd shortly) asked for a short operational doc that explains exactly how Redwood handles post-usage settlement: quarterly true-ups, annual true-up/make-good policies, proration rules when we change tiers mid-term, and whether unused commit can roll forward.

Can you share a concise runbook we can attach to the SOW for our procurement and legal teams? I've attached our internal commit_summary_q3.xlsx to show expected monthly token consumption. High-level questions:
- Will Redwood do quarterly true-ups by default, or is annual only?
- How do you calculate a make-good credit for under-delivery vs. an overage credit for over-usage?
- Do commits that are unused in one quarter roll into the next quarter or only for annual true-ups?
- Timeline: what info do you need from us and when, to align with our fiscal close (12/31)?

Appreciate a short runbook and a sample calculation we can send to Procurement.

Best,
Aisha Geller
Head of AI Products
Nimble Health

Attachment: commit_summary_q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Geller <aisha.geller@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit settlement process — next steps and ask

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear ask and for the sheet. Helpful context.

Short answer up front: we support both quarterly and annual true-ups; default for Renewals/SMB deals is quarterly settlement, but for a committed annual contract we can do an annual true-up with quarterly checkpoints. Below is a succinct runbook sketch; I'll attach a cleaner PDF after internal ops sync.

Runbook (summary):
1) Reporting cadence: Redwood publishes monthly usage statements (day 5 of next month).
2) Checkpoints: Quarterly checkpoint reports (Q1/2/3/4) are reconciled within 20 business days after quarter close.
3) Annual true-up: final reconciliation occurs after last quarter; make-goods applied or overage invoices issued within 30 days of annual reconciliation date.
4) Make-goods vs overage: make-good credit = max(0, committed_tokens - actual_billed_tokens) * effective_unit_price; overage invoice = max(0, actual_billed_tokens - committed_tokens) * overage_unit_price (overage unit price is typically list price unless a negotiated cap is in the SOW).
5) Mid-term tier changes: we prorate committed tokens on a daily-utilization basis and apply a blended unit price for the period; the runbook includes a worked example.
6) Roll-forward policy: unused quarterly commit can be rolled forward only if explicitly included in the SOW; otherwise unused tokens are eligible for a year-end make-good only.
7) Dispute windows: Customers have 30 days to raise usage disputes with supporting logs; Redwood will investigate and produce corrected statements if needed.

Plan: Vanessa and Marissa will add operational timelines and a sample calculation. I'll send a formatted runbook (PDF) and a one-page procurement summary today. If Procurement needs a DocuSign amendment, we can provide a SOW addendum template.

Does this align with what Procurement needs? If so, confirm and we'll prepare the SOW addendum language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jake Turner <j.turner@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 13:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit settlement process — next steps and ask

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the kind of summary we needed. A couple follow-ups from Procurement:

- Roll-forward: Procurement prefers unused quarterly commit be eligible to roll into the next quarter up to a 10% cap. Is that a standard optional clause?
- Make-good timing: Can make-good credits be applied to the next invoice rather than issued as a cash credit?
- Dispute SLA: We need a written SLA for the 30-day dispute window and an escalation path to a named Redwood contact if we don't hear back.
- DocuSign: Jake (cc'd) will own the amendment. Can Redwood provide a one-page amendment that adds a roll-forward clause and clarifies billing mechanics?

If you can send a sample amendment and the PDF runbook, Procurement will review and revert by 10/10 to keep us on track for a 12/1 start.

Best,
Aisha

Hi Aisha / Jake — looping in operations details below and attaching the runbook PDF (redwood_runbook_draft.pdf) plus a sample amendment language snippet for your DocuSign flow.

Operational timeline and answers:
- Roll-forward clause: We can add an optional roll-forward of unused quarterly commit up to 10% for the next quarter. We'll include this as a negotiable checkbox in the SOW addendum.
- Credit application: Make-good credits are typically applied to the next invoice for convenience; if you prefer a cash refund we can arrange that but it requires finance sign-off. We'll default to invoice credit unless you request otherwise.
- Dispute SLA & escalation: 30-day dispute window; ops escalation path: first response within 3 business days, full reconciliation within 20 business days. If unresolved, escalate to Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) who will coordinate an executive review.
- DocuSign amendment: attached is a one-page amendment with the roll-forward checkbox and proration formula. It references the deal id NH-2027-042 and includes the sample blended-rate example below.

Worked example (simplified):
- Committed: 100M tokens / quarter at $0.0008 per token
- Actual: Q1 = 85M, Q2 = 110M, Q3 = 95M, Q4 = 120M
- Q1 under-delivery make-good (if roll-forward not enabled): (100M - 85M) * $0.0008 = $12,000 credit applied at annual true-up or to next invoice if agreed.
- If roll-forward enabled (10% cap): up to 10M tokens can roll to Q2, reducing Q1 make-good and offsetting Q2 overage.

Next steps:
1) Karthik / I will send the finalized runbook PDF + SOW addendum for DocuSign by EOD.
2) Nimble Procurement to confirm roll-forward checkbox and credit preference (invoice vs cash) by 10/10 so we can meet a 12/1 go-live.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call with Jake if helpful.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
